sections.Spacecraft and Station: You can't travel to any new worlds, strange or otherwise, if you don't have a starship, so it's no surprise that Spacecraft and the station ability make their return in this set. From the iconic ships of the early days of the Federation to the cutting-edge marvels leading the way after the Burn, an entire fleet of favorites awaits you. 0273_MTGTRK_Main: U.S.S. Enterprise-D, Galaxy-Class Spacecraft is an artifact subtype. Each Spacecraft starts out as just that: simply an artifact, but most of them can become artifact creatures with the help of your brave crew. Most have two striations in their text boxes, while a few have three. They start with any abilities in the topmost striation. But they're kind of stuck at Spacedock until they become creatures. That's where station comes in. Station is an activated ability that can be activated only as a sorcery, meaning during your main phase when the stack is empty. To activate a station ability, you tap an untapped creature you control other than the Spacecraft itself (if it's also a creature). The creature you tap can be any other untapped creature you control, including one that just came under your control this turn. As the station ability resolves, put a number of charge counters equal to the creature's power onto the Spacecraft. Once the Spacecraft has a number of charge counters on it equal to or greater than the number indicated in the circle on the left side of its text box, it becomes an artifact creature with the power and toughness indicated on the right side. It will also gain any abilities in that striation. For example, once the Enterprise -D has seven or more charge counters on it, it becomes a 4/5 artifact creature with flying and vigilance while keeping its triggered ability and station. Not all Spacecraft become creatures once they reach the indicated number of charge counters. If there is no power and toughness indicated, it simply means the Spacecraft will have the abilities listed in that part of the text box. It won't become an artifact creature.
sections.Assimilate: Say, you look like someone with biological and technological distinctiveness. Perfect. 0001_MTGTRK_CommNew: The Borg Queen The Borg share a group consciousness. They operate with one mind, focused on one goal: seek perfection by assimilating other species into their Collective. Assimilate is a new keyword action that brings one of your opponent's creatures over to your side. Resistance is futile. Most cards that assimilate will instruct you to assimilate a card that isn't on the battlefield. To do this, put it onto the battlefield under your control with a +1/+1 counter on it. It is a Borg artifact creature and will lose any other creature types it would otherwise have. If the card has any supertypes, card types, or subtypes other than creature types, it will keep them. If you're instructed to assimilate a creature that's already on the battlefield, you first gain control of it, then put a +1/+1 counter on it. It becomes a Borg artifact creature and loses all other creature types it has. Again, if it has any supertypes, other card types, or subtypes other than creature types, it will keep them.
sections.Battlefront (Commander Only): Commander is a perfect environment for a Klingon craving the thrill of battle. There are so many enemies to attack! Surely, songs will be sung of your victory—maybe even an entire opera! Battlefront abilities reward you for doing what you were born to do: attack multiple opponents in the same turn! Qapla'! 0004_MTGTRK_CommNew: Worf, Defiant Commander Battlefront is an ability word used to highlight abilities that care about the number of opponents you attacked this turn. This number will be used in different ways, depending on the specific battlefront ability. To attack an opponent means to declare one or more creatures as attacking that opponent. Creatures that enter the battlefield attacking won't count. For example, if you attack a single opponent with a creature that has myriad, the number of opponents you attacked that turn is one, even though the token copies fanned out and went after each other opponent. If there are multiple combats in a turn, battlefront abilities will remember who you've previously attacked. For example, say you're in a game with three opponents, and in one combat phase you attack one opponent with Worf. Worf's ability will trigger, and you'll exile one card. If there's another combat phase that turn and in that combat phase you attack the other two opponents, Worf's ability will trigger again, this time exiling three cards. If instead in that additional combat you attack the same opponent you attacked in the first combat and one new opponent, Worf's ability would exile two cards. Note that an opponent you attacked twice in a turn counts only once for battlefront abilities.
sections.Seek Out (Commander Only): Star Trek teaches us to seek out not only new life outside of ourselves, but the best versions of ourselves. But in Magic games, sometimes you just want to seek out more cards to do cool stuff with. 0003_MTGTRK_CommNew: Jean-Luc Picard, Luminary Seek out is a new ability word that highlights triggered abilities that trigger whenever you draw your second card each turn. These abilities will trigger even if the permanent with the ability wasn't under your control as you drew the first card. So, if you draw Jean-Luc Picard, cast him, then draw a second card that turn, his seek out ability will trigger. Find a way to draw two cards during an opponent's turn, and the ability will trigger again. Before you know it, your opponents will be left scrambling while you can relax behind a hand full of cards, a board full of colossal threats, and a nice cup of Earl Grey.
